rationale: Tests recall of ICHD-3 minimum attack number required for migraine without aura diagnosis, a foundational criterion students must know.
Tests understanding of the SNNOOP10 red flag criteria — specifically whether 'thunderclap onset' is a red flag requiring urgent investigation.
Tests application of migraine preventive therapy thresholds — specifically whether propranolol is a first-line preventive for qualifying patients.
Tests ability to identify the single most discriminating feature that differentiates primary from secondary headache during history-taking.
Tests ability to identify papilloedema as the key sign of raised ICP on fundoscopy during headache evaluation.

Tests understanding of the differential diagnosis principle that a new-onset thunderclap headache in an older patient requires exclusion of secondary causes before attributing it to a primary headache disorder.
Tests knowledge of LP contraindications — specifically whether thrombocytopenia is an absolute contraindication.
Tests knowledge of the key differentiating CSF finding between bacterial and viral meningitis — the predominant cell type.
Tests the key diagnostic distinction between traumatic tap and true SAH on CSF analysis — the most important clinical interpretation challenge.
Tests application of acute migraine therapy — specifically the preferred route for a patient who is vomiting and cannot take oral medication.
Tests understanding of the medication-overuse headache (MOH) trap and the first-line preventive approach.
Tests knowledge of empirical antibiotic regimen for community-acquired bacterial meningitis in an adult — a critical emergency medicine fact.
Tests understanding of medication-overuse headache (MOH) — the most important counselling point for migraine patients taking frequent analgesics.
